reasoning: Formal drops ω>0, but it is a pure generalization (like Mathlib's Function.Periodic): for every ω>0 it is exactly the informal notion; domain ℝ and equation match.

Uses Mathlib's PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology, whose closed sets are exactly zeroLocus S = V(S), and defines Zariski closure as closure in it. Only doubt: the source may mean classical varieties in k^n rather than Spec.

RelativelyPrime is defined as True (vacuous), g,h are global functions rather than coprime germs, and ZeroSet never requires g(z)=0, so every point of U with a local representation is in the "zero set".

v(0)=⊤, ultrametric inequality, multiplicativity on units and surjectivity onto ℤ are all present. getD looks lossy, but the unit homomorphism law with y=1 forces v(x) to be finite for every x≠0, so v really maps K* onto ℤ.
Simple = InjOn [a,b]; closed simple = InjOn [a,b) plus z a = z b; quasi-simple = injective off a finite set. All three match. Continuity of a "curve" is ambient and not part of these definitions.
Literally encodes "either true or false, but not both" for a Prop. The informal notion is meta-level (declarative sentence) and has no deeper formal content to capture.
`Set String` has nothing to do with Einstein's index convention; it is a placeholder.

Stability condition matches: every non-matching edge e has f∈M sharing a vertex v with e <_v f, and the preference order is a parameter. That M is a matching is left to the caller, a generalization of the adjective "stable".

The informal refers to an unseen equation (1). The formal gives the standard meaning (c-Lipschitz with c<1), which for a linear operator A is equivalent to ‖A‖<1. The source may intend another variant.
Vector space structure, associative multiplication and both bilinearity laws match exactly. A module over a field on an AddCommMonoid is automatically a group.
The first k rows and columns via Fin.castLE. Allowing k=0 is a harmless generalization.
`def V : Sort* := sorry` has no content.

Takes the "equivalent" condition θ(H_i)=E_i as a hypothesis, drops the defining hypothesis θ(E_i)=H_i (an unused variable is not included), and assumes nothing that makes E,H generate Λ. The resulting lemma is not the informal claim.
Requires f and its local inverse g to be C^1 on all of ℝ^n (global ContDiff), which is strictly stronger than f being C^1 on W and f|U being a C^1 diffeomorphism onto f(U).
Componentwise order on the product, 1=(1_0,1_1), i0 and i1 as defined. Preorder is the usual forcing notion of p.o.
Edge G is a subtype of *ordered* pairs, so every edge appears twice, as (u,v) and (v,u). The copies share vertices and must get different colours, which inflates the number to ≥2Δ+1.
c divides a and b, and every common divisor divides c. Dropping "nonzero" is a harmless generalization.
Sheaves are modelled as bare fibrewise type families, and the "isomorphism" is a plain Equiv of dependent function types: not O-linear, not a sheaf iso, and no restriction to U as a sheaf.
The informal is an unfinished Isabelle stub ("Complete this") with no semantics. The formal invents a meaning (reflexive-transitive r-closure intersected with X) that the source does not determine.
P is unused. Edges are arbitrary sets of index pairs not derived from P's tropical curve, and there is no graph Ṽ(P). Only the gcd-max arithmetic resembles the informal.

The Prop is vacuous: the NormedRing/NormedAlgebra instances already force continuous bilinear multiplication. They also add things the informal lacks (submultiplicative norm, unit), so the defined notion is not the informal one.
A two-argument K-valued map, linear in each variable with the other fixed. Ring instead of field is a generalization.
Excursion and positive excursion match, and "negative otherwise" equals W<0 throughout for continuous W. Z copies the informal sup formula literally, though over s∈ℝ rather than the intended range.
The family h_t has no continuity in t, so any homeomorphism with h_1 K1 = K2 qualifies. This is ambient homeomorphism rather than isotopy, and makes e.g. a knot equivalent to its mirror image.
RightWDepOn (a i) is applied to the whole family a, not to a_1..a_{i-1}, which trivializes or changes the condition.

The evaluation map x ↦ (f ↦ f x) is right, but it uses real-valued C(X,ℝ) where the source's C(X) is complex (a Banach algebra with character space ΔC(X)), and the codomain is bare functions rather than characters.
The vector-space triple is right, but the algebra's multiplication has none of the conditions of 2.1.12 (bilinearity, associativity) that the informal requires.
h should be a ℂ-antilinear isomorphism E ≅ E*, and ⋆̄ is antilinear. The formal uses ℂ-linear maps, no isomorphism, and a plain linear TensorProduct.map.
The empty set.
Scope runs from after the summation sign to the first delimiter: '=', ± at the same bracket depth, or a ')' whose '(' precedes the sign. This matches the four rules (end of formula is the list end).
Entrywise conjugation via star.
Decreases conformal weight by 1 is encoded as H(T* a) = H a − a, which is wrong (it should be [H,T*] = −T*). dY is an arbitrary function rather than ∂Y, and there is no vertex-algebra structure.
Mathlib's Complex.exp is defined as this power series, and the lemma records agreement with Real.exp.
No p ≠ 0 condition: the zero polynomial makes every real number "algebraic".
Exactly the two stated axioms (triangle in the given form, and d(x,y)=0 ↔ x=y).
Row insertion bumps the first entry > k, appends if none exists, and recurses into the next row or creates a new one. Faithful to the RSK description.
K.Normal means normal in G, not in S i. There is no properness (S(i+1)=S i is allowed), no start at G or end at ⊥, and no finite length.
μ is defined on all subsets instead of a σ-algebra 𝓑. That is a substantively different (and much more restrictive) notion.
RationalFunction is an arbitrary function, so the condition is trivial. Char p uses the p^m power instead of the 1/p^n root.
IsAbelianExtension := True, so this is the composite of all intermediate fields (all of K).

The degree n is restricted to ℕ, while the informal (an ODE-style homogeneous function) allows any real degree. This is a restriction, not a generalization: e.g. degree −1 or 1/2 cannot be expressed. Otherwise it matches.
`orthogonal : Prop` is an unconstrained field (vacuous), and τ is a bijection of all of Γ rather than an orthogonal bijection Γ1→Γ2.
Every PDE notion is defined as True; the forms of the equations are never encoded.
The linear change of variables and the transformed form f'(x',y') = f(αx'+βy', γx'+δy') are encoded faithfully. The determinant condition does not affect the definition of the transformed form.
Injection, bijection, and strict ≺ = ≼ and not the reverse (the informal's third line has an obvious typo, and the formal follows the intended meaning).

Δ = {α : (α|α)=2} and root lattice = ℤ-span of Δ is everything. The form B is a parameter; positive definiteness and integrality are hypotheses on the input, a generalization that agrees on intended inputs.
The informal requires T_i M_i = M_i. The formal only has T_i M_i ⊆ M_i, a weaker invariance condition that is not obviously equivalent (T is not assumed surjective).
SigmaOneIdeal is an arbitrary ideal, so the Σ₁ restriction is dropped and this becomes an ordinary PID.
Int.ModEq n a b is by definition a % n = b % n, i.e. same remainder.
The declaration has both [Preorder S] and [CompleteLattice S], two unrelated orders, so Monotone and sSup can refer to different ≤. It also restricts general posets to complete lattices.
g•x = x → g = 1: no non-identity element has a fixed point. That is exactly a free action.
Denumerable = infinite and (at most) countable = countably infinite, and countable = finite or denumerable.
2×2 matrices whose determinant ad−bc is a unit.
An m×n matrix as a function Fin m → Fin n → R.
x ∈ E and some ball meets E only in {x}.

The morphism condition is exactly the informal's characterization: pullback sends O(Y) into O(X). AffineVariety is modelled abstractly as a carrier of regular functions, which is all the definition uses.
Completely incoherent iff autocoherence = 0. Autocoherence is taken as given, as in the informal.
F(r•x) = r^m F(x) for r>0 and x≠0, with real m.

The smoothness and polynomial×derivative boundedness conditions are right, but the functions are ℝ-valued, while the source's Schwartz space (on which the Fourier transform acts bijectively) is of complex-valued functions.
h ≠ h' ⇒ some q ∈ Q and g : b→q with h≫g ≠ h'≫g. The cogenerator is the singleton case.
Every coefficient function is constant in x.
a | b iff ∃ c, b = a c over ℤ.
Every element of Frac(A) that is integral over A lies in the image of A.
The informal defines the notion as "T* = ∅". T* comes from earlier context and the formal takes it as given.
{b | ∀ a∈A, ab = ba}.
∃ C with |φx−φy| ≤ C|x−y| on S. A general metric domain is a harmless generalization.
∅ ∈ 𝒞 and S is a countable union of members of 𝒞.
Coherent sequences as a subgroup of the product: θ_n(a_{n+1}) = a_n.
Distinct inputs have distinct images.
Nonunit, and u | st ⇒ u | s ∨ u | t, exactly as stated.
Both definitions match: full-measure forward-invariant sets, a measure-preserving φ (with a measure-preserving inverse ψ for isomorphism), and the intertwining law on X'.
∃ measurable A with ν1(A) = ν1(X) and ν2(A) = 0.
D = (c1−c2)(c1−c3)(c2−c3) and discriminant = D², in terms of the roots.
Generating = span is ⊤; finitely generated = spanned by a finite set; basis = generating and linearly independent (the informal's stated equivalent).
All four separation axioms are transcribed exactly.
The smallest subfield of ℂ containing F and all roots of f, which is F(α1..αd): the splitting field inside ℂ.
v ≠ 0 and Av = ηv for some scalar η.
The theta series term by term, (−1)^{βn} e^{πiτ(n+α/2)²} e^{2πiv(n+α/2)}, summed over n∈ℤ.
h = g·a for some power series a.
Finite support, for both sequences and I-indexed families (0- vs 1-based indexing is immaterial).
∀ε>0 there is a point of E other than p within ε of p.
Products ∏U_i with each U_i open and U_i = X_i for all but finitely many i.
A combination with not all coefficients zero that sums to 0.
Closed under increasing unions and decreasing intersections of sequences.
Mathlib's adj.homEquiv is σ: (L A ⟶ B) ≃ (A ⟶ R B). Unit = σ(id), counit = σ⁻¹(id).
f ∘ n with n strictly increasing and n_k in the domain {m, m+1, …}.
Functors F and G, unit, counit, and both triangle identities in the standard form.
The induced subgraph is connected, and C is maximal among vertex sets with connected induced subgraph.
{x | x ∈ U ∧ x ∉ A}.
Uses (⊤ : Ideal B).jacobson, which is ⊤, not the Jacobson radical (⊥.jacobson). The quotient is trivial, so every algebra is "basic".
The sum is the sup of the submodules, and direct means M_j ⊓ (sum of the others) = 0 for every j.
(D1)–(D3) are not shown. The formal gives the standard metric axioms (nonnegativity, identity, symmetry, triangle), which is what they must denote.
The four listed axioms, verbatim.
The ideal spanned by all products xy with x∈I, y∈J.
Contains ∅ and X, and is closed under binary union and complement.
Irrational, and a root of a genuinely quadratic (a≠0) polynomial with rational coefficients.
dom₁ = {u : K(u,v) > −∞ ∀v} and dom₂ = {v : K(u,v) < +∞ ∀u}, over an ordered codomain with ±∞ (a generalization of extended reals).
range A = ker B.
A bounded linear map between complex Hilbert spaces that is norm-preserving and onto.
f[k] = ⟨f 0..f(k−1)⟩ ∈ T for all k, and a binary path is ℕ → {0,1}.
Cauchy–Schwarz for n real pairs, stated exactly.

Stated for a noncommutative `Ring`, where it is false. In the artinian ring M₂(k), the nilpotents E₁₂ and E₂₁ span the whole ring as a (left) ideal, so no power is ⊥. The informal is about commutative rings.

The integrals `∫ x in E, f n x` are taken against the default Lebesgue measure (volume), not μ. Only finiteness of μ(E) and integrability are w.r.t. μ, so the statement mixes two measures. It is also restricted to ℝ.
Compact ⇔ closed and every ε admits finitely many ε-balls covering K, in a complete metric space.
The answer to "is f continuous?" is no, and the formal asserts ¬Continuous for the same f.
The class of 0 mod 4 equals the set of multiples of 4, which is the example's content.

The conclusion demands a zero in the *open* ball ‖x‖<r. The source (Evans) means the closed ball, and the open version is false: n=1, v(x)=x−r. The norm on Fin n → ℝ is also the sup norm, not Euclidean.
C(2n,n) ≤ 4ⁿ/√(πn) for n ≥ 1.
ab ≤ εa² + b²/(4ε) for a,b,ε > 0.
LeftLimit, RightLimit and FourierSeries are `sorry` placeholders, and "strongly piecewise differentiable" is ad hoc (one-sided derivatives within Iᶜ). The statement has no real content.

`Continuous H` for H : X → ℝ → X is continuity into the product (pointwise) topology, i.e. each H(·,t) is continuous, with no joint continuity or continuity in t. "Contractible" becomes trivially true of every space.
∫₀^∞ (3t² + 5cos 4t) e^{−st} dt = 6/s³ + 5s/(s²+16) for s > 0.
Bounded is encoded as ∃ p : X, …, which is false when X is empty (K = ∅ is compact). The formal theorem is unprovable, although the informal is true.
Only the real case is stated. The source's normed spaces ("linear manifold", Halmos/Berberian style) are complex, and the complex Hahn–Banach is not a direct corollary of this statement.
N_G(P) ≤ H implies N_G(H) = H and [G:H] ≡ 1 (mod p).

All limits are taken along nhdsWithin c (Ioo a b), which contains c when c is interior. That is not the punctured limit x→c, so the hypotheses constrain f, g and f'/g' at c, and the conclusion forces (f/g)(c) = 0/0 = 0 = L.
For arbitrary I and nonempty A the claim is false (I(w)=w on (0,1)). The informal relies on the ambient coercivity and weak lower semicontinuity assumptions, which are dropped.

It only compares two hand-written formulas that are algebraically identical. Neither the chi-square distribution (the law of a sum of squared normals) nor a Gamma distribution object appears, so the lemma's content is lost.
CompleteBipartiteGraph and spanningTreeCount are arbitrary variables, so the statement is meaningless (and false in general).
x ∈ closure A ⇔ every open δ-ball around x meets A.
Linearity of expectation for finitely many finite-range (simple) random variables. The integrability hypothesis is automatic in the probability setting and harmless for general μ.
x² = 1 for all x implies the group is abelian.
The claim is that the one-point compactification of X∖{x} is homeomorphic to X. The formal instead says x is not isolated (X∖{x} is dense), a different statement that is false for finite discrete X.
Formula 4 is formalized as ∀x∀y (r(y,x) ↔ ¬r(x,x)), which is not valid (the intended Russell-style formula is ¬∃y∀x(…)). Formula 3 also fails for empty α.
A convergent real sequence is bounded.
u is an arbitrary function, so the claim "u is bounded and Lipschitz" is false. The value-function context (from which the bounds follow) is dropped.
y = 4e^{2t}+3 satisfies y' = 2y − 6, the example's answer.
A×B is the six pairs and A×∅ = ∅.
It only asserts that a max and a min exist. The actual answer (max 100 at (±10,0), min 0 at (0,0)) is never stated.
A two-sided inverse ring hom exists, which is equivalent to f⁻¹ being a ring homomorphism.
Upper triangular (A i j = 0 for i > j) implies det = ∏ A i i.
The vectors are dependent and v3 = 2v1 − v2, both as in the solution.
isWeakSolution is an arbitrary predicate, so the statement is vacuous or false. The PDE (1) is absent.
The passage's conclusion: every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) is x² + y².
Domination by an integrable Z plus convergence in measure gives L¹ convergence. It is stated for a general measure, which is still true and specializes to the probability case.

The kernel claim quantifies over *all* y : ℝ → ℝ using Lean's junk `deriv`. It fails at the singular point x=1: gluing a₁x+b₁eˣ and a₂x+b₂eˣ with b₁≠b₂ and a₁+b₁e = a₂+b₂e gives a C¹ solution (deriv² junk = 0 at 1) outside the span. The formal statement is therefore false.
For a locally finite family of open sets, the closure of any subunion is the union of closures.
Only square n×n matrices are covered. The informal's content is the rectangular case (C m×n, D n×m, differing identity sizes), which this does not imply.
min on ℕ is commutative and associative.
∏_p p^{−v_p(a)} · |a| = 1, i.e. ∏ over all places of |a|_v = 1.
Graph, Planar, minor, K5 and K33 are arbitrary variables, so the statement is meaningless and false in general.
D_N_star is an arbitrary nonnegative real, not the discrepancy of ζ, and I is an arbitrary set (it should be the unit interval). The formal claim is false.

No differentiability is assumed on y, and Lean's `deriv` is 0 at non-differentiable points. Gluing c₂t²ln t with different c₂ on either side of t=1 (y(1)=0, y'' junk = 0 at 1) satisfies the equation but is not of the stated form. The ⇒ direction is therefore false.
The Ico case allows a = b (and similar degenerate cases), giving s = ∅, which is not IsConnected (that requires nonempty). The formal theorem is false.
The number of handshakes among n people is C(n,2), and the formal states C(n,2) = n(n−1)/2.
The homology groups H are an arbitrary family unrelated to R, Q, P. Pairwise-trivial intersections of three submodules do not give a direct sum, and the maps are arbitrary. The formal claim is false.
The existential topology q is never used: IsOpen and Continuous resolve to Mathlib's existing quotient instance, so q plays no role and the construction or universal property is not expressed.
A is open ⇔ A = interior A.
χ and ε_La are arbitrary functions, so the formal claim is false. The specific character and representation are absent.
Every additive subgroup of ℤ is nℤ for some n ∈ ℕ. The converse (nℤ is a subgroup) is built into the statement.
(ZMod p)ˣ is cyclic for prime p.
V, Z0, L and sl2F are unrelated abstract modules and the hypotheses don't connect them, so the formal claim is false.
Characteristic function and infinite divisibility are arbitrary predicates, and ψ is wrongly required to itself be a characteristic function.
Only the side remark h ≠ 0 is formalized. The main claim, that h is a homotopy from the unit circle to the square (continuity and the endpoint maps), is missing.
g₄ and g₆ are arbitrary functions on an arbitrary field, so the claim is false (g₄=g₆=0 gives 4X³). The lattice-invariant context, where the discriminant is nonzero, is lost.
(α,δ)-conjugacy is invented incorrectly (A = PBP⁻¹ + (α+δ)I), and the skew polynomial ring K[t;α,δ] is replaced by an ordinary polynomial ring over matrices.
IsTransient := sorry, and the hypothesis ∑ₙ p_ij(n) = 1 is nonsense for transition probabilities.
Arbitrary f and c, with pointwise equality assumed as a hypothesis, so the theorem is just funext. The specific integers f_{αβ}, c_{αβ} are absent.
The informal ("Prove Proposition 3.6") has no content, and the formal is an arbitrary Prop variable.
IsDeltaSystem is wrong: with t ⊆ D, s = D ∪ t = D, so it says all sets are equal. A Δ-system needs pairwise intersections equal to a common root.

IsLocalMax/IsLocalMin are over ℝ-neighbourhoods, so at an endpoint of J the behaviour of u outside J (unconstrained) decides it, and the first claim can fail. The strict-monotonicity strengthening is omitted. The equation also uses junk `deriv` without assuming pu' is differentiable.
Consistent, MaximallyConsistent and HasHenkinProperty are arbitrary predicates, so the statement has no connection to Lemma A.16's construction.
ZMod n with ring multiplication is not the cyclic group C_n: h^e = 1 counts ring roots of unity. For n=8, e=2 there are 4 solutions (1,3,5,7) but gcd = 2, so the formal claim is false.
IsOrientationPreserving and IsIsotopy are `sorry`, and the example's "twist" is not specified.
The conclusion (every φ_j is injective) is assumed as a hypothesis, and φ is arbitrary rather than the contraction maps. It is circular.
Only asserts that the det = 1 elements form a subgroup of GL_n(R) for one ring R. Representability of the kernel functor by a scheme is absent.
X is the plane, not the circle. Paths are arbitrary ℝ→X with no loop condition, and the conclusion is mere reflexivity (α ~ α), not triviality of the group.

The source uses forcing posets (ℚ is a p.o., "dense" means every q has some p ≤ q in IP, and dense embeddings preserve incompatibility). The formal instead uses the rationals with metric density, and h_suborder has an unbound z.
The informal is Tonelli for nonnegative terms, with values in [0,∞]. The formal works in ℝ and adds summability of every row and column as hypotheses, a strictly weaker statement.
The informal is about Riemann integrability. The formal uses IntervalIntegrable (Lebesgue) in both hypothesis and conclusion, so the theorem "the uniform limit is Riemann integrable" is not captured.
U is an arbitrary map, so the claim U(e^{ikt}) = k is false in general. The winding/index functional is not defined.
A₀, A₁ and P are arbitrary, and the hypotheses about P never connect to A₀ or A₁. The claim is false.
Det_q is an arbitrary function, so multiplicativity is false in general. The quantum determinant and quantum-matrix hypotheses are absent.
PID is encoded without IsDomain, and the statement is then false: in ℤ/6 (a principal ideal ring, not a field), ℤ/6⧸(3) ≅ F₃ is a field but 3 = 3·3 is not irreducible.
Encodes that 0 (⊥) and M (⊤) are submodules. The terminology is not a claim. Trivial but faithful.
Homotopy groups, suspension, connectivity, CW and iso/surj are all arbitrary variables (MorphicMap is undefined), so the statement has no content.
The product of two covering maps is a covering map.
The conclusion is `True`. The informal is only a hypothesis fragment, and nothing of the theorem is stated.
The informal factorization is truncated, and the formal claims x^15−1 = (x+1)(x²+x+1), which is false (degree 15 vs 3).
FTA is stated for every nonzero polynomial, which is false for nonzero constants (degree ≥ 1 is needed). The odd-degree part is fine.

Adds a complement-closure hypothesis (univ∖A ∈ R), which turns the ring of sets into an algebra. That restriction excludes e.g. rings of bounded sets, so the formal is a strictly weaker statement than the proposition.
Finite-dimensional subspaces of a real normed space are closed. The complex case follows directly by restricting scalars.
The indicial polynomial is mistranscribed: p₂(0)·(r−1) instead of p₂(0)·r(r−1). It gives 4 at r=3, so the stated roots and factorization are false.
The orbit lives in [0,1)^d ⊂ ℝ^d, so its closure is never all of ℝ^d and the claim is false. The independence hypothesis also omits 1 (θ=1/2, d=1 satisfies it but is not minimal).
`∑'` of non-summable lengths is 0 in Lean, so intervals of divergent total length make the bound trivial. The question about covering all of ℚ is also omitted.
No theorem at all, just a structure for short exact sequences. The informal's conclusion (6.6.15.2) is missing too.
Every group is a `sorry` type, and the conclusion ∃ iso, True between placeholders has no content.
U₀, K, γ, π, Z and the W-action are arbitrary. The "even" subring ignores the 2P ∩ Q condition, and the claim is false in general.
P is an arbitrary function, and a unique maximizer need not exist. The physical system is absent.
Asserts a presentation whose kernel is the image of M itself (Exact g f), which is stronger than "finitely presented" and false. Over ℤ×ℤ with M = ℤ×0, any g lands in ℤⁿ×0, but ker f ⊇ 0×ℤⁿ.
{∅, Ω} is closed under the operations and contained in every such family, hence is the smallest σ-field. Binary unions suffice for this two-element family.
The informal is garbled (a complex disk D(0,1), D(0,r) → N_r). The formal proves only "uniform ⇒ pointwise" on [−1,1] ⊂ ℝ, which does not capture the stated example.
δ₁ and δ₂ are arbitrary, so the claim is false. The two definitions of δ(z,w) are absent.
The product of two countably infinite sets is countably infinite.
Uses Algebra.adjoin (finite type as an algebra) instead of field-extension generation, a much stronger hypothesis (it forces K/k finite). There is also no IsScalarTower tying E between k and K.
unitSphereVolume is `sorry`, and the index is shifted (n+1 vs n).
S_rank is `sorry`, and G (the algebraic group) and Γ (the lattice) are conflated.
Pi = R₊ ∩ R₋ = ∅ by disjointness, so the simple roots are wrong. The Weyl group action is arbitrary, and there is no root system.
The right side integrates over the image with n-dimensional Lebesgue measure (zero for curves when n ≥ 2), not arc length. The identity is therefore false.
Strictly upper triangular n×n implies Nⁿ = 0.
